verdict.rationale: Paddle's own docs describe API keys with granular permissions that limit a key to specific entities and actions. The MCP docs recommend least-permission API keys for agents, live OAuth MCP connections start with read-only access, and sandbox keys only authenticate against sandbox endpoints. Missing for 10: independent or hands-on corroboration of scoped agent keys, and evidence of key expiry/TTL or per-agent credential lifecycle controls beyond rotation.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can issue scoped/least-privilege API credentials for an agent

citations.quote: Permissions grant an API key access to specific entities or allow it to take specific actions in Paddle.
with hard scoping via least-permission API keys recommended
Live OAuth connections start with read access
Sandbox API keys are prefixed `pdl_sdbx_` and only authenticate against sandbox endpoints
